Rand Paul raises questions about COVID-19 transparency ahead of Fauci testimony
J. I. Wood
Senator Rand Paul, who chairs the Senate Committee on Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs and is a practicing ophthalmologist, shared several posts on July 22, 2026, discussing upcoming testimony by Dr. Anthony Fauci and concerns regarding the handling of COVID-19 information.
In a post made at 15:29 UTC, Paul wrote: "Great night Monday with @MAHA_Action. We're ready to see what Fauci has to say Wednesday. @DrOzCMS https://t.co/8w7p84NIut".
Later that day at 16:20 UTC, he posted two additional messages. The first stated: "documents here: https://t.co/eI6z9DW6Xd". In another message posted at the same time, Paul said, "COVID cronies and the Intel Community were more concerned about protecting the CCP than being honest with the American people. They even talked about it amongst themselves on Slack. https://t.co/oK0s3mwYCj".
Senator Paul is known for his medical background; he earned his degree from Duke University School of Medicine and works as an ophthalmologist, having founded the Southern Kentucky Lions Eye Clinic (official website). He also performs pro-bono eye surgeries in Kentucky and internationally and assists Kentucky residents with federal government matters. As chair of a key Senate committee, Paul's comments often attract attention in discussions related to public health policy and government oversight.
